title: Dragon's Lair
build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

records.c: The first copied byte in the scene record is $08. The caller starts executing one byte later.
Disable the sprites and load file LI through $0334 with selector 9. Set up two transfers, select the VIC bank at $4000 and multicolour bitmap mode, then request sound $82.
After LI returns, copy $8216–$8600 to the colour matrix at $6000 and $7600–$79EA to colour RAM at $D800. Configure multicolour bitmap mode in the $4000 VIC bank.
Clear the runtime page at $0400 and set the sprite colours, pointers and coordinates from four tables at $30E9–$3108.
Update the two background regions selected by $0414 and service the scene delays between copies. The branch at $1F69 chooses between two event paths based on $0433.
The ending text builder saves its descending character index here before reading the glyph selector at $2202.
Twelve ending glyph selectors. The setup replaces the first five with low palette nibbles from $B006 through $B002 with bit 7 set. The high bit controls the glyph source at $2205.
Read five bytes at $B002–$B006 in reverse order, extract the colour nibble and write the results into the display scratch bytes at $21D7.
Save the destination pointer around the calls that draw the pixel pairs, then advance its base by sixteen and continue with the next column.

Use the calculated destination in $7D/$7E and row values in $81/$82. Write two adjacent bytes at offsets 0 and 1 and two more at offsets 8 and 9, then advance the starting pointer by two. The four-position sequence then advances to the next row.
Read the next source byte, shift its high bits out in sequence and expand each set bit to a two-bit multicolour pair. Return the output bytes through $81 and $82.
Save Y in $46 and call $2934 once per countdown step. An initial zero wraps and runs 256 calls.
Save 65 bytes from the sprite area at $6800 into RAM at $0458, copy in the new image from $A9F9 and set sprite 4 enabled and expanded.
Store A in $0444, apply the bitmap and sprite update helpers and jump to the display routine at $2934.
Copy from ($65) to ($67) inclusive through the source limit given in X/Y. Increment both pointers after each byte that precedes that limit.
Copy a byte from the source pointer at $65 to the destination at $67. Stop after copying the source address given by $041C and $041D. Otherwise advance both pointers with carry into their high bytes.
Set copy source high byte from X and low byte from Y.
Set copy destination high byte from X and low byte from Y.
Use A to select a pointer from $31C5 and a source index from $31CB. Copy sixteen bytes backward from the table at $3195 to that destination.
Read CIA1 port A into $0407 and test the player Y and movement gates. Merge the position-dependent bits on the affected paths.
Merge the outcome bits in A into $0407 and return.
Return to the caller. The alternate position path enters at the next instruction, $2367.
Set bits 0 and 2 of $0407 and return through the shared movement exit. The boundary tests use the player X high bit and the low X limit $20.
Increment $041F and use its low two bits to gate updates. When the action flags allow, toggle the four-sprite pose bank and load the pointers from $30AF before returning through the raster IRQ exit.
Jump to $268D from this raster dispatch path.
Tick the extra sprite sequence. Test sprite 0 position and phase flags to begin the upper-screen event, clearing sixteen bitmap bytes at $4228 and requesting sound $8D on entry.
Run the region check at $2693, then advance the frame pointer at $044F between $CB and $CD while the animation flag is set. Use $0454 for the delay and $0453 for direction.

Read the VIC collision latch and save sprite 7 position and pointer. If $0450 is set, display the alternate yellow sprite at the coordinates in $044D/$044E. Advance sound before leaving the raster phase.
While the countdown at $0457 is nonzero, decrement it and put sprite 7 at X=$130, Y=$E0 with pointer $CF.
When $0420 is set, restore sprite 7 coordinates and frame from $044A–$044C and colour it white. If $0435 is active, inspect bits 5 and 7 of the VIC sprite collision latch to select a reaction.
Check the motion gates before updating the player, then advance the active sprite 7 frame between $90 and $92. Tick the sprite-pair event and the temporary background and scroll effect when enabled.
Advance sprite 5 and 6 pointers by two. Disable the pair once the first pointer reaches $97 and reenable it with pointers $93 and $94 when it reaches $99. Update their colour and timer together.
Restore CPU registers and return from the raster interrupt.
Update the sprite 4 animation, then test the gates at $043D, $0424, $042D and $0435 before comparing Dirk's low X, high X and Y with the selected trigger bounds.

Compute the difference between $73 and $5F, compare it with $75 and order the two magnitudes into the step numerator and denominator at $77/$78. Set $7C to select the dominant direction and clear the remainder.
Decrement the colour timer. Reload it to five at expiry and choose colour 2 or 7 from the current colour nibble. Advance the sprite movement twice before falling through into the movement helper.
Check the activity flag at $0435. Use the direction flags to select a low-X or Y step. On rightward wrap set the high-X bit for sprite 5 and mark it in $043B.
Add the numerator at $77 to the remainder at $79. When it meets the denominator at $78, subtract that denominator and apply the secondary coordinate step under the current direction flags.
Compare sprite 5 Y against $7A and branch to $2840 if it is below the threshold.
Set sprite 5 to colour 2 and frame $98. Flag the completion, save the sprite coordinates, clear its motion gate and request sound $88.
Shared early return for the sprite 5 screen-coordinate bounds tests.
Reject sprite 5 when its high-X bit is set, when its Y after subtracting $21 is outside $80–$DF, or when its low X equals $FF. Otherwise offset the coordinates and prepare the bitmap probe.

Decrement the sprite timer at $0428. On expiry inspect the event selection at $040F and the current sprite 4 pointer. The routine can enable the sprite and switch between frames $C6 and $C7, or clear its enable bit and reload the longer delay.

Read the current phase at $0418 and patch the jump at $2914 from the split address tables. Advance the phase modulo five, install its compare line at $D012 and acknowledge the VIC interrupt before jumping.
Synchronize with the shared raster wait, install $28EF in $42/$43 and select the first compare line from $305E. Reset the phase index and acknowledge the VIC interrupt flags.

When $0448 is set, use the saved X and Y selectors and test the $0451 gate before loading the paired values at $317E and $3181. Call the room patch routine at $2E56 and clear the pending flag. Then check the separate trigger at $0426.

Test the position in $5F against $60 through $82 and require sprite 5 high X. With the event gate clear, request sound $8C, set the high-X bits for sprites 5 and 6 and select frame pointers $93 and $94.
Poll $63FC until it equals $50, then double A for the picture selector table lookup.

Double A to index the source-address tables. Select eleven 144-byte bitmap strips for index 6 or five 56-byte strips for index 8, set the first destination and tail into the position and transfer setup at $2A15.
Write the chosen high byte of the copy destination to $2B18. Set $2AEA to $60, or take the neighboring entry at $2A0B to select destination $4040.
Use Y to select the sprite 4 position and three pairs of patchable copy operands from the tables at $30BB, $30C7 and $30D3.
Copy the two indexed colour sources into the screen matrix and colour RAM. Advance both destination operands by forty bytes at each patched row width and stop at the patched source count.

Read corresponding values from the two patched sources and write them through the two patched destinations. The code advances the destination operands by 40 after each 16-cell group until X reaches $B0.
Choose one of two bitmap sources by doubling the selector at $0414. Copy six 56-byte strips from that source to bitmap rows starting at $4B68.

Copy each strip backwards from the patched absolute source to the patched bitmap destination, using Y as the last offset. Advance the source by $4D and the destination by $140, repeating for X plus one strips.

Read and write one strip via the patched operands, counting Y down through zero. Advance the source by the stride at $4D and the destination by 320 per completed strip. Keep copying until the signed decrement of X ends the loop.
Reset the animation step and enable the motion gate before the first retreat update.

Update the scene, then increment the animation index at $0443. Use the vertical step table at $3184 below index $11 and apply three leftward coordinate updates. At the limit clear $0403 and leave through $2BB4.
Use the larger quartet index while the animation step is from 4 through 12. Fall through to install that step's four pointers.
Copy four player frame pointers from the indexed group beginning at $309F to the primary sprite pointer slots. Set the step to one and mark the mirror flag.
A return between the bitmap copy loop and the next entry at $2BB5.
Select the destination by doubling A. Clear five rows through the zero-fill helper, then apply the palette for source index zero.
Clear bit 7 of the VIC sprite enable register while preserving the other seven bits.
Set bit 7 in the VIC sprite-enable register, preserving the other sprite enables.
Load $F0 into countdown $0457 and run two calls to the shared display delay at $1869.

Refresh input and position limits. If the movement gate is clear and the delay has expired, toggle the walk pose index and test the four active-low direction bits. Apply the relevant pose, orientation and displacement to the player sprite group.
Set the shorter delay and choose an oriented four-sprite standing pose from $308F or $3093 according to the last direction in $0404.
Add the horizontal step at $040B to sprite 0 low X and give the result to all four player sprites. Set their high-X bits on carry and restore A before returning.
Subtract the horizontal step at $040B from sprite 0 low X and give the result to all four player sprites. Clear their high-X bits on borrow and restore A before returning.
Test the gate at $042F and player high X. When the gate is set and high X is clear, check the low X limit before selecting the position test or merging movement mask 5.
Zero both contact state bytes at $042F and $043A before returning.
Set $043A when the player sprite coordinates fail the range checks.
Double A to select the source word from $3132. Patch the bitmap copy to draw two 43-byte strips beginning at $4D7B.
Save the row width index in $3136 and write zeros down through index 0. Advance the patched destination by 320 and use X to count the rows.
Use A to select the bitmap destination and Y to select the source. Y zero takes the erase path. Otherwise copy four strips of forty bitmap bytes, then apply the paired colour patch.

Use the destination from the table at $313D and the sources from $3143 and $314B. Configure the shared compositor for twenty cells, five per row. Patch its exit to return after copying, then restore the original exit opcode.

Disable interrupts and derive the probe coordinates from sprite 0 and the direction-indexed offsets in $3063 and $3067. Pass the adjusted coordinates and saved horizontal carry to the address calculator.

Save the low three vertical bits for the scanline within a cell. Divide the vertical coordinate by eight, combine the horizontal byte and saved carry to obtain the column, and multiply the row by $A0 before assembling the bitmap address.
Store A, Y and X in the first three bytes of the scratch page beginning at $0400.
Load A, Y and X from $0400, $0401 and $0402 respectively.
Store A, Y and X in that order at $0442, $0441 and $0440 so the caller can recover them after scene work.
Recover A, Y and X from $0442, $0441 and $0440. The final X load determines N and Z.
Copy sprite 0 low X to sprites 1–3. Give sprite 1 the same Y as sprite 0 and place sprites 2 and 3 $15 lines below it.

When active, count down $042C and advance the frame index in $042B. For the six frames load positions and pointers for the pair of sprites from the tables at $306B, $3077 and $3083. Finish by hiding both sprites and clearing the sequence flags.
Low bytes of five phase handler addresses patched into the jump at $2914. The index comes from $0418.
High bytes of the same five handlers, paired by index with the table at $3054.
Five VIC raster compare values $00, $33, $80, $DA and $F8. The dispatcher advances its phase before installing the next compare.
Four horizontal offsets selected by $0404. The contact sampler subtracts the selected value from sprite 0 X at $2EEB.
Four vertical offsets selected by $0404. The contact sampler adds the selected value to sprite 0 Y minus fourteen.
Six pairs of coordinate offsets. The update at $2FA3 subtracts the even entry from the base X at $5E and adds the odd entry to the base Y at $5F.
Six pairs of VIC sprite pointers for sprites 5 and 6, indexed by the sequence counter at $042B.
Six pairs of offsets from sprite 5 to sprite 6, applied to the X and Y coordinates after the first sprite is placed.
Sprite pointer records read by the movement routines at $2D36 and $2BAA. The values run from $9E through $C5.
Two little-endian addresses of the sources selected by $0414 for the recurring bitmap-strip update.
Six little-endian source addresses installed in $2B14/$2B15 for the self-modifying copy at $2B13.
Six address pairs patched into the second read operand at $2AC4/$2AC5 by the sprite-location selector.
Six address pairs patched into the first read operand at $2ABE/$2ABF by the selector at $2A15.
Five pairs of position bytes assigned to $D009 then $D008 by the selector at $2A15.
Initial colours for sprites 0–7. The set-up reads them at $1ECB.
Initial sprite frame pointers copied at $1EC8 to the eight-byte table beginning at $63F8.
Initial low X coordinates for each sprite. The register loop at $1ED4 uses an even register index.
Initial Y coordinates for each sprite. The register loop at $1EDA writes the odd register address.
Three triplets loaded into VIC sprite pointers 0–2 by the scene loop at $2025.
Three low X coordinates loaded into sprite 0 by the scene animation. The other sprites take the same low X from $2F87.
Three Y coordinates for sprite 0. The grouping routine then derives the other three Y coordinates.
Three delay parameters loaded into X at $2008 by the intro animation.
Three corresponding delay parameters loaded into X at $200B.
Sixteen pixel bytes copied in reverse order to $4228 by the setup at $1F2F.
Four masks indexed by current direction. The code at $2E02 merges the selected bits into $0407.
Two source pointers selected by A at $2E0E. The copy draws two strips of 43 bytes to $4D7B and the next bitmap row.
Y value saved before the zero-fill loop and reloaded before the next row.
Three bitmap destinations used for the small scene patch and its zero-variant fill path.
Three screen matrix destinations. The compositor uses the same low byte and adds $78 to the high byte for the colour RAM destination.
Four little-endian screen matrix pointers indexed by twice the variant. The nonzero variants read packed colour pairs here.
Four little-endian colour RAM pointers indexed by twice the variant. The nonzero variants read their third-colour bytes here.
Four little-endian bitmap sources indexed by twice the patch variant. The nonzero variants copy four strips of 40 bytes.
Twenty $FF bytes at the bitmap source address stored in the first word of the table at $3153. The zero-variant clear has its own entry at $2BB5.
Three pairs of low-X thresholds indexed by the even trigger selector. The comparisons at $26CD and $26D2 include the first bound and exclude the second.
Three high-X comparison bits selected by halving the trigger index.
Three counters initialized in the loop at $1F3D and decremented by the event position test.
Three Y-coordinate bounds compared by the event position test at $288C.
Three byte values copied into $044D when the pending patch matches its saved selector.
Three companion values copied into $044E under the same condition.
Seventeen signed vertical offsets indexed by the retreat animation at $2B69. The sprite update subtracts the selected value from low Y.
Three sixteen-byte background masks used by the cell restoration routine at $232E.
Three little-endian cell destinations selected by doubling A at $232F.
Three offsets $2F, $1F and $0F select the last byte of each 16-byte source mask at $3195.
The clear path at $2BB6 saves twice the selector here before setting up the bitmap destination. Reload it at $2BD4 to select the corresponding palette destinations.
Three VIC pointer bytes copied to the final three sprite slots at $63FD–$63FF.
Three colour values $0E, $01 and $01 copied to $D02C–$D02E.
Six interleaved low X and Y bytes copied to the coordinate registers for sprites 5–7.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
First $400 bytes of the dragon-room bitmap, laid out as eight consecutive raster bytes per screen cell.
Dragon bitmap cells 128 through 255, selected by $D018 bit 3 clear and bank $4000.
Source pixels for dragon bitmap cells 256 through 383, after the dragon scene enters bitmap mode.
Dragon bitmap cells 384 through 511, paired at display time with the colours in the screen matrix.
Dragon bitmap cells 512 through 639. In multicolour mode each byte encodes four two-bit pixels.
Dragon bitmap cells 640 through 767, one byte per cell scanline.
Dragon bitmap cells 768 through 895 for the lower section of the screen.
Final 104 cells of the dragon bitmap from $5C00 through $5F3F.
Two 43-byte strips read by the short patch at $2E0E for selector zero. The first destination is $4D7B and the next is 320 bytes later.
Eighty-nine multicolour pixel bytes remain after the two copied strips and before the zero-filled end of the bitmap bank. They are outside its 8,000 visible bytes.
The last 17 bytes before the screen matrix at $6000 belong to the 255-byte zero run in the disk picture stream starting at $9BAA, which extends through $60ED.
The dragon room bitmap begins at $4000 in VIC bank $4000. The scene uses $6000 as its screen matrix, selected by high nibble 8 in $D018.
Image at VIC pointer $90. The initial pointer table at $30F1 selects this frame for sprite 7.
Frames $91 and $92 for sprite 7. The raster updater at $25BE advances its pointer from $90 to $92 before the direction changes.
Frames $93–$98 for sprites 5 and 6. The update at $261B steps the even and odd pointer sequences and controls when the sprites are visible.
Three sprite frames addressed by $99, $9A and $9B in the event pointer pairs at $3077.
The last 64-byte image slot referenced by the paired raster event table at $3077.
A 64-byte sprite shape at pointer $9D. The pixel mask forms a low cloud, between the raster event frames and the player pose bank.
Sprite fragments for pointers $9E and $9F. These are the first two immediate slots in the pose pointer data at $308F.
The sprite image addressed by pointer $A0 in the $4000 bank. Sprite 4 selects this image in the dragon play capture.
Sixteen 64-byte fragments following the live sprite 4 slot. These are within the scene pose sequence whose pointers begin at $308F.
Middle bank of dragon-scene character parts, addressed by the sequential $B1–$C0 pointers stored in the pose table.
Five final sequential 64-byte fragments indexed through the pose table ending at pointer $C5.
Two 64-byte frames addressed by pointers $C6 and $C7. The tick at $28B3 changes between them while keeping sprite 4 enabled.
Three image slots selected by the pointers $C9, $C8 and $CA loaded for sprites 5–7 at $2182.
Three frames for sprite pointers $CB–$CD. The raster updater at $246C advances and reverses the pointer saved in $044F.
The tall sword-shaped mask at VIC pointer $CE, between the alternating upper-band sprite frames and the bonus text sprite.
Image selected by pointer $CF for the lower-band sprite at $24FA.
Three 64-byte image slots selected through the pointer triplet $D0–$D2 in the table at $3109.
Five 64-byte frames for pointers $D3–$D7, selected through the scene animation table at $3109.
Inclusive source of the copy to $D800 made at scene start. The routine copies these bytes into the VIC colour RAM for the bitmap.
Small patch variant 3. Four strips of forty bitmap bytes copied at $2B13.
Small patch variant 3. Four rows of five packed screen colours copied at $2AC3.
Fifth row of five packed screen colours. The small patch copies four rows, leaving this row before the paired colour RAM record.
Small patch variant 3. Four rows of five third-colour bytes copied at $2ABD.
Fifth row of five third-colour bytes followed by one zero before variant 2 pixels. The copy takes the first four rows.
Small patch variant 2. Four strips of forty bitmap bytes copied at $2B13.
Small patch variant 2. Four rows of five packed screen colours copied at $2AC3.
Fifth row of five packed screen colours before the paired colour RAM source. The copy takes the first four rows.
Small patch variant 2. Four rows of five third-colour bytes copied at $2ABD.
Fifth row of five third-colour bytes followed by one zero before variant 1 pixels. The copy takes the first four rows.
Small patch variant 1. Four strips of forty bitmap bytes copied at $2B13.
Small patch variant 1. Four rows of five packed screen colours copied at $2AC3.
These five packed colours complete the 25-cell variant 1 matrix allocation at $7C31–$7C49. The active copy stops after four rows.
Small patch variant 1. Four rows of five third-colour bytes copied at $2ABD.
Fifth row of five third-colour bytes followed by two zeros before the opening palette source. The copy takes the first four rows.
The 176 screen matrix bytes that the opening picture update copies into eleven rows of sixteen cells starting at $6008.
Eighty zero bytes after the eleven copied screen-matrix rows. They fill the remaining five 16-cell rows before the opening colour RAM record.
The 176 colour RAM bytes paired with the opening screen matrix patch. The indexed load at $2ABD feeds eleven rows starting at $D808.
Five blank 16-cell rows complete the opening colour RAM allocation before the variant 1 screen matrix.
The 176 screen matrix bytes selected by bitmap variant 1. The compositor copies sixteen cells per row starting at $6008.
Five zero-filled rows after the portion of the variant 1 matrix used by the opening compositor.
The first third-colour bytes selected by bitmap variant 1, whose full source runs through $8014. The compositor copies sixteen cells per row starting at $D808.
The final 21 bytes of the variant 1 third-colour record, continuing from $7F65.
Five 16-cell zero rows after the variant 1 colour RAM record and before the variant 2 matrix.
The 176 screen matrix bytes selected by bitmap variant 2 for rows starting at $6008.
Five 16-cell zero rows between the variant 2 screen matrix and its paired colour RAM.
The 176 third-colour bytes selected by bitmap variant 2 for rows starting at $D808.
One zero byte between the end of the variant 2 colour record and the initial screen matrix source at $8216.
The first 1002 bytes copied to the screen matrix at $6000. The VIC takes two non-background colour nibbles per displayed cell from this matrix.
Five 56-byte pixel strips copied starting at $4DF0 by selector 4. The first byte is also the inclusive end of the initial screen palette copy.
Two 56-byte zero rows follow the five strips copied by selector 4. The following palette record starts at $8788.
Thirty-five packed colour pairs written by selector 4 to the screen matrix from $61BE. Each full row is seven cells wide.
Two seven-cell rows of packed colours follow the five rows copied by selector 4. They complete the 49-byte screen-matrix record.
Thirty-five third-colour bytes written by selector 4 to colour RAM from $D9BE. Each full row is seven cells wide.
Two seven-cell rows of third-colour bytes follow the five rows read by selector 4.
One zero byte after the seven-by-seven final third-colour record.
The first seven 144-byte strips in the selector-3 bitmap patch. They start at $48F0 and advance $140 bytes per strip.
The final four 144-byte strips in the selector-3 patch. The first of these writes to $51B0.
198 packed pairs of bitmap colours copied by selector 3 to the screen matrix starting at $611E. The paired transfer advances $28 bytes per row.
A single $FF between the 198-byte packed screen colour and third-colour records for the large patch.
198 bitmap colour bytes copied by selector 3 to colour RAM starting at $D91E. The copy writes up to eighteen cells per row.
Thirteen zero bytes immediately before the six-strip patch selected at $8FB5.
Six 56-byte strips selected when $0414 is zero. Their first bitmap destination is $4B68.
The companion six strips selected when $0414 is one. The destination positions match the alternate image at $8FB5.
The first eight 128-byte source strips of the opening patch. The indexed copy at $2B13 lays them into the bitmap from $4040 with a destination stride of $140.
The last three 128-byte strips of the opening patch. Their bitmap destinations begin at $4A40, $4B80 and $4CC0.
Sixteen zero bytes between the opening bitmap strips and the start of selector 1 at $97E5.
The beginning of the eleven 128-byte bitmap strips for selector 1. The destination advances by $140 for each strip starting at $4040.
Continuation of the selector 1 bitmap source at $97E5. The LI file supplies this portion.
Sixteen zero bytes between the end of selector 1 and the first bitmap strip of selector 2 at $9D75.
The first portion of the eleven 128-byte bitmap strips for selector 2. The destination starts at $4040.
Continuation of the selector 2 source from $9D75, through the end of the data loaded from LI.
Final portion of the selector 2 bitmap source, read directly from the LH staging area following the LI load.
Eighteen bytes of complete LH tokens between the two direct bitmap operands. They expand to $6FAD–$6FE5 inside the player pose sprite bank.
The first eight 128-byte source strips for selector 5, read directly from retained LH bytes and copied into rows starting at $4040.
The final three bitmap strips for selector 5, continuing the record from $A307.
The 176 screen matrix bytes paired with bitmap variant 5. The opening-patch compositor copies them to eleven rows starting at $6008.
Byte $07 separates the 176 copied screen-colour bytes from the 176 copied third-colour bytes. It is also a literal in the LH packed picture stream.
The 176 third-colour bytes paired with bitmap variant 5. The opening-patch compositor copies them to eleven rows starting at $D808.
Seventeen literal LH tokens after the 176 bytes copied from the variant 5 third-colour source. They decode to $78F0–$7900 in the initial colour RAM source image.
Source for the 65-byte replacement at $6800 copied by $22A9. These bytes survive in the packed LH file staging region after LI loads.
Five bytes read backward by $21E7. The display preparation extracts their low nibbles.
Data read by $2AC3 for X from 0 through $AF during the two-source picture copy.
The companion 176-byte source read by $2ABD in the same X loop.
Final tokens of the LH picture stream. The first token expands across $99FF–$9A01, and subsequent tokens continue through $9A71. LI replaces the decoded pixels from $9A00 onward.
